literal: Than poverty, is more painful possession of wealth, if one falls under the scepter of a king who does not do justice.
translation: If one must live under the scepter of a king who does not administer justice, possessing wealth is far more painful than suffering poverty.
modern: நீதி செலுத்தாத அரசனுடைய செங்கோல் ஆட்சியின்கீழ் வாழ நேர்ந்தால், வறுமையை விடச் செல்வத்தை உடையவராக இருப்பது அதிகத் துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the dread of living under an unjust ruler. The poet states that if a person lives under a king who does not deliver justice ('முறை செய்யா மன்னவன்'), having wealth ('உடைமை') becomes a greater source of misery than poverty ('இன்மை'). Under a tyrannical regime, the wealthy are constantly targeted, extorted, or harassed, making their possessions a liability. Thus, the pain of holding wealth under tyranny far exceeds the hardships of having nothing at all.
